title: New Zealand cyclone wind — the 2023 season
summary: Peak 10 m gust per hex cell across Cyclones Hale and Gabrielle. Checked against the IBTrACS best-track archive rather than assumed, exactly two named storms came within 600 km of New Zealand in 2023: Hale in January, which passed within 2 km of the coastline, and Gabrielle in February, whose damage fell mainly on Hawke's Bay and Tairāwhiti. Both windows are analysed here.
body: The index is the highest 10 m gust each hex cell recorded during those events. Cells are hexagons of 30 km circumradius — 60 km wide and 52 km tall — clipped to the coastline. The payout question is about wind over land, so an ocean cell reading 200 km/h is a picture of the sea, not a claim.

This POC was originally scoped on a parametric windfield: cyclone best-track points driving a Holland vortex, the method used in production for Caribbean hurricane microinsurance. That does not survive contact with the New Zealand record. Gabrielle carries no intensity and no radius-of-maximum-wind at any of the 30 track points across its approach, and only three points in twenty-six years within 300 km of the coast carry both. The cause is institutional, not a data gap: the agencies that publish radius-of-maximum-wind have no responsibility for New Zealand, and the agency that does has never published the field. No alternative feed fixes that, so the hazard is reanalysis instead.

The ladder attaches at 110 km/h and reaches full limit at 125, paying on 24 of 112 land hexes in this season. It replaced a first version set to the Australian/NZ cyclone category boundaries, which is correct as a map legend and wrong as a trigger: 63 km/h is a genuine Category 1 boundary and also ordinary New Zealand weather, and that ladder paid on 80 of 112 hexes. There are only two tiers because the index ceilings at 130.9 km/h — a 28 km cell average cannot reach what a headland reaches — leaving 21 km/h above attachment, against a measured 10 km/h gap between the model and real instruments. A third tier would be separated by less than the model's own error.
caveats: ERA5 is a backtest and pricing input. Final ERA5 runs 2-3 months behind and ERA5T about 5 days, so a live product would trigger on station gusts, never on this.
Values are 28 km grid-cell averages. Exposed sites read higher: Auckland airport recorded 88.9 km/h during Gabrielle while exposed capes recorded 150-159 km/h.
Peak over the season's analysed cyclone events, not an annual maximum. A winter storm can out-blow a cyclone here.
No observed New Zealand cyclone loss series exists, so payout-versus-loss is recorded as not applicable rather than estimated.
